description: M04-U7 case index (m04-plan §3, §4; u7-plan §2): every M04 exit case and claim mapped to its Cargo test targets and tests, per platform, in the M02 format (tests/native/m02/case-index.json description; read by tests/native/m04/m04-evidence.py, which is m02-evidence.py with the M04 constants). Patterns resolve into required-inventory.json from the build host's sources, never from run logs. Owner-input rows are blocked_rows naming m03-plan §7's B-IDs (M04 adds none). M04 specifics: the Windows-hosted WSL runs (tests/native/m04/run-mode-b-windows.ps1) are scenario platforms (windows-modeb, wsl-containers, wsl-login, windows-lock) whose scenario_targets are the runner's own `### <plan name>` tests.txt sections and whose steps are the cargo test names printed under them (cargo's `Running` line follows the test output there, so a section is not a cargo target); the Windows-only and Linux-only tests of e2e_platform_m04 (windows::native::* and container::a31_*), which tests/e2e/platform_m04.rs includes with #[path] so that platform-tests.py's source scan cannot name them, are carried by platform_required (exact names that must pass on that platform) and not by the inventory.

heimdall_testkit-unit::repo::tests::unse.reason: asserts that the compile-time repository root (the build host's checkout) holds Cargo.toml and schemas/, which exists only where the binary was built; the HM_REPO_ROOT resolution it covers is platform-neutral and its sibling tests run everywhere

integration_login_entry_m04::macos::.rationale: macOS LaunchAgent round trip (#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]): a plist in a scratch directory bootstrapped into the real gui/<uid> domain under a unique label and always booted out (m04-plan §0's one allowed exception); the Linux and Windows mechanisms are the linux:: and windows:: modules

integration_login_entry_m04::linux::.rationale: Linux systemd user unit round trip (#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]): a scratch unit directory, file only; the real systemctl row is service_login::wsl_login::linux_login_entry_starts_runtime_at_next_login (scenario a08-login-entry in a disposable systemd distribution)

integration_login_entry_m04::windows::.rationale: Windows Run value round trip (#[cfg(windows)]): an injected scratch key under HKCU\Software\HeimdallTest\<unique>, never the real Run key

e2e_route_m04::a15_*.rationale: single-hop ProxyJump and agent-forwarding cases need a forwarding sshd and Unix sockets (#[cfg(unix)]): a harness sshd on the Windows PC (the WSL server) cannot honour AllowTcpForwarding, so the Windows rows are not run there (a harness limitation, never counted as passes); route_rules_through_the_real_binary needs no sshd and runs everywhere (tests/e2e/route_m04.rs header)

heimdall_wsl-unit::channel_tests::.rationale: the helper channel's tests drive the real helper loop (helper::serve) over a UnixStream pair (#[cfg(all(test, unix))]); the helper runs inside the Linux distribution, and the Windows side of the channel is the windows_tests module (scenario wsl-helper-session)

heimdall_wsl-unit::helper::lock::.rationale: the helper's single-holder lock uses Unix file semantics (#[cfg(unix)]); the helper runs inside the Linux distribution

heimdall_wsl-unit::helper::tests::.rationale: the helper's owner-only directory rule is Unix file mode semantics (#[cfg(unix)]); the helper runs inside the Linux distribution

heimdall_runtime-unit::managed_store::li.rationale: live tests of the managed store with real Unix-socket endpoints in a scratch directory (#[cfg(all(test, unix))]); the Windows realization of the same flows is the native Windows run (windows::native::*) and the Mode B scenarios

heimdall_credential-unit::endpoints::con.rationale: the container endpoint is a Unix socket admitted by the SO_PEERCRED uid rule (#[cfg(unix)] module); a container environment's engine runs in Linux

child_entries.e2e_platform_m04::windows::native::handl: child entry point (not #[ignore]d: a no-op unless the probe variables are set; re-executed with --exact by the handle-inheritance cases; never required)

A12.limitation: The A12 flow row's ssh.exe reads the test world's scratch configuration through -F (Windows paths only, ADR-0010 §2 item 3); scp.exe and sftp.exe with Linux local paths are reported unsupported (ADR-0010 §2). The macOS and Linux rows are mechanism evidence (the helper channel against a stand-in helper process); the native rows are the Windows Mode B harness's, run in disposable hm-m04-<hex> distributions only.

A15.limitation: Docker Desktop, devcontainers and WSL-nested containers stay `not-tested` by decision. Routed enrollment evidence lapses at fresh_until (lifted by M06-T03). Existing-access jump has no approved key (I-12). The Windows route rows (a15_* but route_rules_through_the_real_binary) are not run on the PC: the harness sshd has no forwarding settings; that is a limitation of the harness, not an owner input. On macOS a15_forwarded_endpoint_bounded_to_binding passes by returning early when the host's sshd (OpenSSH 10.1 or later) places forwarded-agent sockets under the account's ~/.ssh/agent (it prints `blocked (B3 ...)`): that pass is not forwarding evidence and the macOS platform_required list leaves it out; the Linux row (devbox sshd 9.6p1) runs it. The container engine rows run in one disposable WSL distribution with Podman and Docker Engine installed inside it only.

honest-limits.title: plan §5 M04 exit: unsupported clients, architectures and Docker Desktop are separately labelled; the tests below prove the limits M04 states (refusals of an unsafe run base, a lost helper relaunch rule, routed enrollment and existing-access jump limits, the sandboxed-profile state directory)
honest-limits.note: Known limits carried into the exit draft (u7-plan §4): Mode B plain `ssh <alias>` needs `ssh -F` or GIT_SSH_COMMAND (no ~/.ssh/config projection, I-11); routed enrollment evidence lapses at fresh_until unless verified while reached directly (lifted by M06-T03); the existing-access jump has no approved key until M06-T03 (I-12); a background relaunch racing a stop can still be started once (R03 ruling); Mode B refuses a base with a group-writable ancestor or a non-root symlink (set XDG_RUNTIME_DIR); a sandboxed Windows profile makes a pre-M04 state directory state_dir_unsafe (platform fact); Docker Desktop, devcontainers and WSL-nested containers are `not-tested` by decision; other §10 and §11 residuals (spawn-lock window, a forwarded-agent row that needs sshd < 10.1 or a scratch account (B3), no per-pair route status (M07-T03), login-entry console flash, Mode B leftovers across a restart, re-issue at a higher generation fails closed, the helper does not enforce the deadline, Bridge::drop up to 2 s, the bridge supervisor holding the store after a managed runtime's drop on Windows) are recorded in the exit draft, not asserted by a test.
